Package io.mavlink4j.session

Interface TxScheduler

All Superinterfaces:
AutoCloseable
All Known Implementing Classes:
DirectTxScheduler
public interface TxScheduler extends AutoCloseable
Runs named periodic TX tasks (heartbeat emission, RC override relay, ...) on one shared thread pool rather than one hand-rolled thread loop per feature, so every periodic sender shares one thread lifecycle.

  • Method Details

    • pooled

      static TxScheduler pooled(MavlinkSettings settings)
      A scheduler backed by its own small thread pool (MavlinkSettings.txPoolSize() threads from MavlinkSettings.threadFactory()), for a caller that wants one outside a MavlinkSession — a session already owns one, see MavlinkSession.scheduler(). The caller owns it and must close() it.

    • repeat

      TxScheduler.Handle repeat(String name, Duration period, Runnable task)
      Runs task every period, starting immediately, until the returned TxScheduler.Handle is closed. A task that throws is logged and the schedule continues — one bad periodic task must never silently stop firing without a trace, and must never take down another task sharing the same scheduler.
      Parameters:
      name - used only for diagnostics (thread naming, log messages) — not an identity key

    • submit

      void submit(String name, Runnable task)
      Runs task once, as soon as a pool thread is free — the latency-sensitive counterpart to repeat(java.lang.String, java.time.Duration, java.lang.Runnable) for a TX path that must not wait for the next tick of a periodic task (a stick that moves 1 ms after a tick should not pay a full period for a clock that had no reason to be where it was). Same catch-and-log contract as repeat(java.lang.String, java.time.Duration, java.lang.Runnable) — a task that throws is logged and never reaches the pool — and the same "already shut down" tolerance: a submission racing scheduler shutdown is dropped, not thrown, since callers submit from threads that must not fail on teardown.

      No TxScheduler.Handle is returned: a one-shot that has already been handed to the pool cannot usefully be cancelled, and every caller re-checks its own state when the task actually runs.

      Parameters:
      name - used only for diagnostics (log messages) — not an identity key

    • close

      default void close()
      Releases the threads this scheduler owns; idempotent. A scheduler that borrows its threads has nothing to release, hence the no-op default.
      Specified by:
      close in interface AutoCloseable
